newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Put spread sold in FTSE as shares surge.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Put spread sold in FTSE as shares surge.

text.p: The surge in the UK stock market on Tuesday prompted a large deal to be struck in FTSE 100 index options, dealers said.

The deal meant buying out-of-the-money puts in American style FTSE and selling puts in European style FTSE so that if the index remains above the options strike prices at expiry, the options will be worthless and seller of the spread would reap a reward equal to the net credit from the sale.
The deal involved buying 7,500 March 4050 puts at 3p and selling 7,500 March 4125 puts at 6-1/2p making a net credit of 3-1/2p.

Another large deal in FTSE options was the sale of 1,000 March 4425 calls at 10-1/2p but dealers were not sure whether this was hedge position -- to protect a portfolio of stocks in case the cash market weakens -- or a purely speculative one which expects the FTSE to be capped at 4425 by March expiry.
By 1505 GTM, the FTSE 100 index was up 42.2 at 4349.3.

Over in stock options Standard Chartered Bank was busy mainly owing to a crossed trade -- in which a broker acts for the buyer and seller of options which are traded at one price, and the broker collects two commissions.
The deal was for 1,600 April 950 calls in Standard Chartered to be traded at 12p. Standard Chartered shares had jumped up 24p to 890p.

Elsewhere, in electricals company GEC a straddle was the main deal and it concerned buying 500 May 390 calls at 14-1/2p as well as 500 May 390 puts at 18-1/2p which will make money if the underlying shares either fall below 357p or they go above 423p by May expiry.
